page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m4.xlarge is an entry-level shared compute instance based on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz, the virtual machine provides 4 vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware acceleration flags include AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA. The instance includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence, and provides a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It contains no dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture optimized for moderate, non-continuous compute demands. The server achieves average single-core performance scores, demonstrated by 1539.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1733.69 in stress-ng single-core tests. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics rank in the lower quartile, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 3455.0 and PassMark CPU scoring 5906.83. Memory throughput reflects average performance during large uncached transfers (42.27 GB/sec read and 28.56 GB/sec write), but cached access speeds and database operations sit in the lower percentiles.

Because the ecs.e-c1m4.xlarge relies on shared vCPU allocations, it prioritizes resource economy over sustained compute throughput. The lack of bundled local NVMe storage and modest 1 Gbps networking further position it as a cost-efficient platform for light workloads. It is best applied to standard utility services, lightweight web serving, development environments, and low-traffic internal applications that require 16 GB of memory without heavy multi-threaded execution.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m4.xlarge is a general-purpose shared instance delivering 4 vCPUs across 2 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.5 GHz and 16.0 GB of memory. Operating on KVM virtualization within the x86_64 architecture, it features AVX-512 and AES instructions, 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and relies entirely on remote storage due to the absence of bundled local disks. Benchmark profiles show reliable average single-core compute performance alongside lower-tier multi-threaded and database metrics, characteristic of shared processor resources. Lacking dedicated GPUs, the ecs.e-c1m4.xlarge offers an economical footprint tailored for development environments, low-traffic web applications, staging servers, and background utilities that fit a balanced memory footprint without needing continuous full-core execution.
